Football.title: Brutal Tuchel releases EIGHT players from England camp ahead of Japan game with three stars’ World Cup dream in tatters
Football.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL has swung the axe on his England squad — with eight players sent packing just days before the Japan clash.

The Three Lions boss is trimming his group after the underwhelming draw with Uruguay, as he edges closer to naming his World Cup squad.





Tuchel originally called up a huge 35-man group for this camp – his final chance to assess options before the big decision in May.

But after Friday’s flat showing, the German has wasted no time in reshaping his squad.

A total of eight players have now left the camp, with the group cut down to 27 for Tuesday’s friendly against Japan.

Arsenal pair Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice are among those departing after missing the Uruguay game through injury concerns.

Both remain expected to feature at the World Cup, but have returned to their club for further checks.

Gunners team-mate Noni Madueke has also gone back to north London after picking up a knock during the match.

Manchester City defender John Stones is another big name to exit after suffering an issue in training.

Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton will also miss out after aggravating a problem during his substitute appearance.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Goalkeeper Aaron Ramsdale, defender Fikayo Tomori and striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin have also left the camp, though no official reason has been given for their departures.

Meanwhile, a fresh wave of players, including Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon, are now linking up with the squad after being rested earlier in the international window.

Tuchel’s ruthless reshuffle comes at a crucial moment, with places for this summer’s World Cup hanging by a thread.

And for some of those sent home, their England dreams may already be slipping away.

Football.title: Gordon Banks’ ‘Pele save’ shirt & 1966 World Cup winner medal set to fetch huge sums as memorabilia goes up for auction
Football.content:
THE England jersey goalie Gordon Banks wore to defy Brazil’s Pelé with the Save Of The Century is going under the hammer.

The stopper’s blue top is expected to fetch between £200,000 and £300,000.





Banks turned out in it for a Mexico 1970 World Cup group game in Guadalajara against eventual winners Brazil which the Three Lions lost 1-0.

Banks — who died in February 2019 aged 81 — famously pulled off an acrobatic reflex save to flick away a downward header from Pelé.

TV commentator David Coleman’s screamed: “Pelé! What a save! Gordon Banks!”

The shirt could go for more than the one worn by Pelé in the 1970 Final, which fetched a record £157,750 when it was auctioned at Christie’s in 2002.

Also up for grabs is the ­goalkeeper’s 1966 World Cup winner’s medal valued at up to £250,000.

The shirt and medal are being offered by separate anonymous sellers.

Another England goalie shirt — worn by Peter Shilton in the Maradona Hand of God World Cup 2-1 defeat to Argentina in the 1986 quarter- finals — is also up for grabs.



The grey-and-blue top from the Mexico City game is valued at £200,000 to £300,000.

The items go on sale in person and online from 11am on June 10 through BUDDS in Wellingborough, Northants.

BUDDS’ David Convery called the Banks shirt “iconic”.

He said: “He wore blue in that one match. Gordon wore yellow in the others but Brazil were in yellow, of course.”

Football.title: Cole Palmer’s stunning born-again Christian girlfriend hoping for divine intervention to give him World Cup spot
Football.content:
FOOTIE ace Cole Palmer’s partner Olivia Holder is a devout Christian — and she’s hoping for divine intervention to take them both to this year’s World Cup.

The Chelsea star is sweating over a place in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad, with God-fearing model Olivia saying her prayers that he makes it.





She will doubtless dust off her eye-popping wardrobe for the showpiece tournament as she heads for the US with the other England WAGs, if the 23-year-old Blues forward makes the final cut.

But while her outfits might get plenty of attention, 23-year-old Olivia will also be packing her Bible and prayer book for the tournament in the US, Mexico and Canada in June and July.

Olivia is a regular churchgoer and insists on Sunday morning worship, even while on holiday.

She has shared snaps with thrilled fans, showing her reading the Bible and attending church services.

A source revealed: “Church is a massive part of Olivia’s life. Her faith is very important to her and the Bible is her favourite read.

“Sure, she is a beautiful and glamorous model and influencer, but she knows that beauty is only skin deep.”

Olivia was first seen going on a secret date with Cole last year, and the couple shared snaps of their travels in Dubai.

On Friday night, she and Cole were pictured after the England vs Uruguay friendly at Wembley, in which he came on as a substitute in the 1-1 draw.

Football.title: Arsenal fear TRIPLE injury blow as Declan Rice & Bukayo Saka quit England camp without playing as they join Madueke
Football.content:
ARSENAL are sweating on a TRIPLE injury blow with three players quitting England’s camp.

The FA confirmed Noni Madueke will return to Arsenal.





Like Adam Wharton who will head back to Crystal Palace, Madueke picked up a knock during the 1-1 draw with Uruguay on Friday night.

And the pair have been allowed to depart early from Thomas Tuchel’s final meet-up before the World Cup.

Madueke will be joined back at Arsenal’s London Colney HQ base with key Gunners and England pair Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka.

England posted videos of the pair arriving in camp on Saturday morning.

Rice trained with the team – and James Maddison – at the Tottenham training ground.

But both Rice and Saka reported problems so will not feature in the Three Lions’ second game against Japan.

Instead, the superstar duo are both heading back across North London to their title-chasing club for further medical assessments.



Madueke, who started the game with a bandage on his left wrist, left Wembley in a knee brace after limping off before half-time.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

And that will come as worrying news for Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, who already has Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes, Leandro Trossard and Martin Odegaard all in the treatment room.

The Gunners boss is desperate to return to winning ways after the international break – and maintain their quest for the treble.

Arsenal lost the Carabao Cup final to Manchester City before the pause from club football.

Their first game back is the FA Cup quarter-final at Southampton next Saturday before the first leg against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on the Tuesday.



They do not return to Premier League action, where they sit nine points clear at the top with seven games to go, until hosting Bournemouth on April 11.

Football.title: ‘Very sad and upset’ – England boss Tuchel issues ‘worrying’ Noni Madueke injury update after Arsenal star’s knock
Football.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL has given an injury update on Noni Madueke after his early knock against Uruguay.

The Arsenal winger got the nod to start in the international friendly at Wembley on Friday night.





But after a strong early start, Madueke was clattered by Rodrigo Aguirre in the opposition box, and stayed down.

VAR chose not to intervene in the incident, and despite him trying to carry on, Madueke was soon substituted for Jarrod Bowen just before the 40-minute mark.

Madueke was later seen leaving the stadium in a knee brace, sparking more concern over a potentially lengthy absence for the 24 year old.

Tuchel addressed the injury after the match, but admitted the exact extent of the knock remains to be seen.



Tuchel said: “I’m worried, of course. Very sad and upset and hopefully it’s not a big injury.

“It was the tackle. I think it was on the edge, the tackle, within the box. But they didn’t check it.”

England powered on with Bowen on the wing, and thought they had secured a late win through Madueke’s fellow Gunner Ben White‘s back-post tap-in.

But a wayward foot from the same man was deemed to have clipped a Uruguay boot in the box, to hand Fede Valverde the chance to equalise from the spot in injury time.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Despite the result, Tuchel was full of praise for his side, including Madueke.

He said: “He started well, he was full of energy, he was ready to go.

“Against a team like Uruguay, who rely on one-on-ones, to isolate them, he makes the spaces open up and he could have been a key player for us, which he is.”



The knock could impact Madueke’s chances of making the squad for the upcoming 2026 World Cup.

And in more immediate terms, the blow will have Mikel Arteta sweating as he looks to hold onto Arsenal’s commanding lead at the top of the Premier League table.

Madueke has been a reliable bench option for the Spanish tactician this season behind Bukayo Saka.

It is rotten luck for the side, for whom Madueke was one of a handful of stars playing after six key squad members pulled out of international duty with injury concerns.

Among them were William Saliba, Gabriel, Martin Odegaard, Eberechi Eze and Leandro Trossard.



Mikel Merino and Jurrien Timber are also recovering from injury issues and are racing to be back to bolster the campaign to bring a Prem title to North London.

Football.title: Roy Keane breaks silence after mum’s death with touching five-word message as Man Utd legends flock to pay respects
Football.content:
ROY KEANE has spoken out after the tragic loss of his mother Marie on Friday.

The 79-year-old passed away peacefully at Marymount University Hospital and Hospice in Cork.





Manchester United legend Keane, 54, uploaded a picture of himself smiling alongside his mum to his 2.4 million Instagram followers on Saturday.

He captioned the post with the heartfelt message: “You’ll always be the boss.”

Fans and former team-mates rushed to the comments to offer their condolences.

David Beckham, Gary Neville and Robbie Keane were among the stars to give their well wishes in the replies.

Fans also chimed in with their sincere messages to the former Republic of Ireland international.

One wrote: “She gave you a Mindset the world couldn’t break.. Strong mums raise even stronger souls. She’d be so proud Roy.”

Per a rip.ie post, Marie’s funeral is scheduled for Tuesday March 31, at the Church of the Resurrection, Farranree.

She will then be laid to rest at St Catherine’s Cemetery in Kilcully.



Keane shared his emotional connection to his mum last year when he choked up while showing around a photo of himself with his parents on Stick to Football.

The Sky Sports pundit shared around the picture of him, Marie and his father Maurice – who passed away in 2019 – before getting emotional.

He explained: “You’re on about family, the ups and downs of football. But when you see your family at Wembley after you’ve won a big game…”



The star then trailed off before taking a moment to compose himself, surrounded by his co-hosts and friends Ian Wright, Neville, Jamie Carragher and Jill Scott.

Mark Pougatch led tributes to Marie during ITV‘s coverage of England‘s friendly with Uruguay on Friday.

He was hosting alongside Wright and Emma Hayes when he said: “Everyone here and all of us at ITV sends our condolences to Roy and his family on the sad passing of his mother Marie.

“All of our thoughts are with the Keane family this evening.”

Football.title: Bradley Dack subjected to taunts from EFL crowd over love life after Olivia Attwood pictured kissing Pete Wicks
Football.content:
BRADLEY DACK was subjected to taunts over his love life – after his ex Olivia Attwood was pictured kissing Pete Wicks.

The Sun’s exclusive a week ago showed the former Love Islander kissing TOWIE star and Sunday Roast: The Podcast co-host Wicks in a Soho bar.





Dack and Attwood split in January amid allegations of the footballer’s infidelity.

The Sun revealed how he is back with his ex-girlfriend Emily Rose Moloney, while other women have come forward to say he cheated on Attwood while “married” to Attwood.

However, we also revealed how the pair were never legally Mr & Mrs.

Dack, 32, captained Gillingham in their League Two clash away at relegation-threatened Crawley Town.



And during a stoppage of play just after the hour mark, the home fans gave him stick for his private life saga.

Dack was pleading with referee Edward Duckworth not to send off team-mate Joshua Andrews for a high boot.

But with the incident taking place in the Crawley penalty area and just in front of the hardcore home terrace, the Red Devils supporters seized their chance.

They chanted: “Bradley Dack, she cheated on you.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Dack gave no reaction, knowing he had to be on his best behaviour after picking up a yellow card for a late lunge in the first half.

The home fans called for a red card early in the second half when he tripped Tobi Adeyemo, the third time he had fouled the Crawley striker, but Duckworth was unmoved.

Dack was twice subjected to wolf whistles, too, after a pair of woeful corners sailed over everybody.

Elsewhere, there were a few chants of “cheat, cheat” – but aimed at Dack’s Gills team-mate Max Clark for taking an age over a throw-in.



And Dack’s nightmare week went from bad to worse in injury time as Crawley snatched a 91st-minute winner.

Dack sank down to his haunches as Gillingham fell behind – and there was still time for a second two minutes later as Gillingham suffered a fifth straight defeat.

Asked on Dack’s wellbeing and how he has been around the training ground this week, Gillingham manager Gareth Ainsworth said: “Bradley’s absolutely fine.

“My captain. Great lad. Fantastic person. And, yes, I’ll have him all day.

“Bradley’s a great player. He’s a fantastic player on the ball. I thought he had a good game again.

Football.title: ‘Peak Louis Saha’ – Man Utd icon limps off in pain as he injures himself scuffing shot wide in Legends game
Football.content:
FORMER Manchester United striker Louis Saha was forced off the pitch after a wayward shot in a legends game.

He was playing in a game against Southampton legends at St Mary’s.





The striker, who scored 42 goals for United struck an effort well-wide before requiring medical attention and eventually leaving the field.

One fan reacted to the injury saying: “Louis Saha going off injured after 20 minutes in a charity match is just peak Louis Saha.”

He played for the Red Devils between 2004-2008, describing his exit from Old Trafford as “painful”.

This was due to his injury woes during his time in Manchester – which defined his time at the club.



The Frenchman was joined by various household names on the St Mary’s turf.

His former team-mate Wes Brown was on the teamsheet – he made 362 appearances for United.

Bulgarian icon and fan-favourite Dimitar Berbatov, who scored 56 times during his time at Old Trafford, was also playing.

Ecuadorian cult-hero Antonio Valencia featured in the match – he won two Premier League titles under Sir Alex Ferguson as well as an FA Cup and a Europa League after the Scotsman’s departure.

The Southampton legends team also featured some stars of English football.

Saints hero Matt Le Tissier – widely regarded as the club’s best ever player – was involved in the game.

He made over 500 appearances for the club – scoring 195 goals.

Former Premier League star Victor Wanyama also lined up for Southampton.



He made his name at the club from 2013-2016 – one of the most successful periods in Saints’ history.

He was part of the squad who qualified for the Europa League in 2015.

Portuguese player Pele also featured – he fostered 70 children since retiring from the game.

Football.title: National League clash ends in brawl likened to '3am city centre stuff' as players separated
Football.content:
National League clash ends in brawl likened to '3am city centre stuff' as players separated

National League leaders Rochdale scored a late winner against Sutton United with tempers flaring

View 3 Images Rochdale and Sutton United players clashed

Tempers flared after the final whistle in the National League clash between Rochdale and Sutton United after the visitors came from behind to pick up a hugely important three points in the title race. Just three points separate first placed Dale from second-placed York City, who defeated Woking on Saturday afternoon.

‌



Rochdale had to come from behind to ensure the gap to their title rivals stayed in tact. Sutton had taken the lead through Charlie Bell in the 78th minute, but league leaders Rochdale equalised in the 89th minute through Devante Rodney before 41-year-old Ian Henderson scored in the 97th minute to maintain their grip on the top spot.

‌



With only one automatic promotion spot available in the National League, every point is hugely significant for both Rochdale and York at this stage of the season. Both sides are set to do battle on the final day of the season, which could see the winner of that game crowned champions. Tensions boiled over after the final whistle following Dale's dramatic late winner.

‌



Jordan Henderson claims England fans don't know truth about Ben White after Wembley boos READ MORE :

In footage shared on social media, players from both teams clash in the centre of the pitch before staff from both teams pile in.

View 3 Images Rochdale and Sutton players clashed (Image: X)

Security also made their way onto the pitch to try and diffuse the brawl, while Sutton's Hayden Muller was shown a second yellow card for his involvement in the fracas.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The 24-year-old could also face further disciplinary action if found guilty of any offences in the referee's write up of the game.

Speaking to talkSPORT after the game, Rochdale boss Jim McNulty said the brawl was "just an absolute tear up I think. It reminded me of 3am city centre kind of stuff that you don't really know how it started.

‌



"And then you're finding it difficult to stop because everyone's got hold of each other.

"And there's bodies rolling around on the floor underneath the swell of individuals that all want to suddenly kill each other."

"There's a few scratches and scars," McNulty said when asked about how his players were. "Well, not scars, but there's a few scratches and bruises in there from people being gripped around the necks and whatnot.

‌



"I don't really know in this moment, but everyone seems all right."

View 3 Images Rochdale and Sutton players clashed (Image: X)

Rochdale are back in action on Good Friday when they host relegation threatened Morecambe, who are on the brink of a third successive relegation and lie eight points adrift of safety.

‌



McNulty's side then take on Hartlepool United on Easter Monday, while title rivals York City travel to Boston United and then host Altrincham.

It's a remarkable race for promotion back to League Two, with Rochdale on 98 points after the win over Sutton, while the Minstermen are on 95 points.

Both teams could realistically finish on over 100 points, with one of them potentially missing out on promotion via the National League play-offs. With five games to go, it looks set to go right to the wire.

Football.title: Three Arsenal stars leave England squad as Thomas Tuchel makes ruthless cull
Football.content:
Arsenal trio Noni Madueke, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are among the eight players who've left the England squad. Alongside Manchester City star John Stones and Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton, the FA say that they'll will return to their respective clubs for fitness-related reasons.

Both Madueke and Wharton suffered injuries during Friday's 1-1 draw with Uruguay, prior to which Stones picked up an issue in training. Rice and Saka, on the other hand, will return to Arsenal 'for medical assessment'.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Aaron Ramsdale, centre-back Fikayo Tomori and striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin have been sent home, as Thomas Tuchel welcomes a number of regular players who were rested for the Uruguay friendly. Rice and Saka were among those but won't feature in Tuesday's clash with Japan at Wembley.

The remaining nine - namely Dean Henderson, Nico O'Reilly, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi, Dan Burn, Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane - are all set on the available. Madueke's injury forced him to come off in the first half on Friday.

"I'm worried, of course, because I think he was a difference-maker today," Tuchel admitted post-match. "He started well, he was full of energy, he was ready to go.

"And I think against a team like Uruguay, who relies on one-against-ones, to isolate them there and to go in one-against-ones from every minute out there, the spaces open up and he could have been a key player for us, which he is. Very sad and upset and hopefully it's not a big injury."

As for Stones' setback, the England manager commented: "He's obviously very upset and at the moment he gets my full support because it helps him more than putting more pressure. He was ready to play for City in the last weeks. He was ready to play.

So no risk at the moment. But he has a lot of credit in the bank with me. So. let's hope that he gets fit because it's most important that he finds his confidence."

Football.title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo isn't playing for Portugal, ban suspended for World Cup, Al-Nassr latest
Football.content:
Why Cristiano Ronaldo isn't playing for Portugal, ban suspended for World Cup, Al-Nassr latest

Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal have booked their place at World Cup 2026 but the veteran is not involved for his country during the March international break

View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo won't play for Portugal in their March friendlies (Image: PA)

The March international break will offer Portugal manager Roberto Martinez a final chance to assess his squad before thinking about his selection for World Cup 2026. West Ham midfielder Mateus Fernandes has earned a first call-up and Toluca striker Paulinho could make his first appearance since 2020 but there is no place for injured star Cristiano Ronaldo.

‌



Ronaldo, 41, won the most recent of his 226 senior international caps in November. He has been left out by Martinez for the upcoming friendlies against Mexico and the United States, though, after suffering a hamstring injury playing for Al-Nassr in February.

‌



The Portugal skipper issued an update after missing his club side's last two games. "Getting better every day," he wrote as the caption for a pair of photos from the gym.

‌



Martinez confirmed Ronaldo, along with compatriots Ruben Dias and Nelson Semedo, had been left out for medical reasons. "No, he’s not in danger [of missing the World Cup]. It’s a minor muscle injury," he said of the captain. "Everything Cristiano has done physically this season shows that he’s in great shape."

Assuming he is fit by June, Ronaldo will make this World Cup his last. However, he risked a suspension after picking up a red card in November's qualifying defeat at the hands of Ireland.

‌



He was banned for the final qualifier against Armenia, with Portugal winning 9-1 in his absence. A violent conduct offence brought him a three-game ban - something which could have kept him out of his country's first two group games in North America - but part of the ban has been suspended.

"The FIFA Disciplinary Committee has imposed a three-match ban on Cristiano Ronaldo following his direct red card at the FIFA World Cup 2026 preliminary competition match between the Republic of Ireland and Portugal played in Dublin on 13 November 2025," a FIFA statement read. "The first of the three matches was served in the encounter Portugal v. Armenia played on 16 November 2025.

View 2 Images Ronaldo was sent off when Portugal lost to Ireland in November (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"In line with article 27 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code, the serving of the two remaining matches has been suspended under a one-year probation period. If Cristiano Ronaldo commits another infringement of a similar nature and gravity during the probationary period, the suspension set out in the disciplinary decision shall be deemed automatically revoked and the remaining two matches must be served immediately at the next official match(es) of the Portuguese representative team.

"This is without prejudice to any additional sanctions imposed for the new infringement. The three-match suspension is subject to appeal to the FIFA Appeal Committee."

He sat out two matches, victories over Al-Riyadh and Al-Ittihad, before making himself available for selection again after two demands were met. He scored four times in as many games before picking up his latest injury, with Al Nassr winning all four.

With eight games of the season remaining, Al-Nassr sit three points clear of closest challengers Al-Hilal at the top of the Saudi Pro League table. Ronaldo has scored 21 league goals, four shy of league top scorer and England international Ivan Toney.

Football.title: Roy Keane shares touching five-word tribute to mum Marie after her death
Football.content:
Roy Keane shares touching five-word tribute to mum Marie after her death

Manchester United legend and pundit Roy Keane is grieving after the death of his mother Marie at Marymount University Hospital in Cork, Ireland, following a long illness

View 2 Images Roy Keane with his mum Marie (Image: @officialkeane16/Instagram)

Roy Keane has paid tribute to his mother Marie after she passed away following a long battle with illness. It was confirmed on Friday that Marie had 'passed away peacefully' while 'surrounded by loved ones' at Marymount University Hospital in Cork.

‌



Manchester United legend Keane was close to Marie. He was supposed to be working for ITV as a pundit for England's friendly against Uruguay on Friday at Wembley, but was absent due to the sad news.

‌



He has now shared a photo of Marie on his Instagram account. The caption simply reads: "You’ll always be the boss". It has a similar theme to a post from 2022 which read: “The Only Boss I listen to.”

‌



Keane received a replies from his ex-United team-mates Gary Neville and David Beckham, who both posted heart emojis. There were also supportive responses from legendary runner Sir Mo Farah, and fellow ex-professional players Robbie Keane and Anton Ferdinand.

Marie was a mother of five and a notice announcing her death said she would be "sadly missed by her loving family, sisters Ina, Annette and Josephine, brothers Jack, Leo, Michael and Noel, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, daughters-in-law Linda, Theresa and Mary, brothers-in-law, sisters-in-law, nephews, nieces, relatives, her great neighbours and friends."

Marie lost her husband Mossie at the age of 79 in August 2019, the year after he had suffered a stroke.

‌



A visitation will take place at a Cork funeral home on Monday before mass at the Church of the Resurrection on Tuesday and a burial following at St Catherine’s Cemetery in Kilcully, Co Cork.

View 2 Images Roy Keane has previously shared a photo with Marie (Image: Instagram @officialkeane16)

Speaking on ITV on Friday night before England's 1-1 draw with Uruguay, presenter Mark Pougatch took a moment to send his best wishes to Keane.

Article continues below

He said: "Everyone here and all of us at ITV sends our condolences to Roy and his family on the sad passing of his mother Marie. All of our thoughts are with the Keane family this evening."

Rockmount AFC, Keane's schoolboy club in Cork, were among the first to offer their condolences. They said: "Sincere condolences extended to Keane and Lynch family on the passing of Marie."

Football.title: Man City star Rodri furiously U-turns on Real Madrid transfer comments
Football.content:
Man City star Rodri furiously U-turns on Real Madrid transfer comments

Rodri made headlines earlier this week by opening the door to a transfer to Real Madrid as he approaches the final year of his current contract with Manchester City

View 2 Images Rodri spoke highly of Real Madrid (Image: Onda Cero)

Manchester City star Rodri has attempted to downplay his comments on Real Madrid after revealing that he'd be open to joining his former rivals. Rodri, 29, is out of contract at City in June 2027 and has been linked with a move to the Bernabeu either this summer or next on a free transfer.

‌



The Spain international played for Real's local rivals, Atletico Madrid, earlier this career. "There have been many players who have gone down that path, right?" Rodri said this week while on international duty.

‌



"And especially not directly, but over time. I mean, for me, you can't turn down the best clubs in the world. They have a fanbase that really goes all out for them, and for me, the Bernabeu is always incredible, a stadium that's very imposing."

‌



His comments took up plenty of column inches and have led to criticism. After Spain beat Serbia 3-0 in a friendly on Friday, Rodri fired back.

"I'm used to it," the midfielder laughed. "If, out of a 50-minute interview, they cut out whatever they want... in the end, I don't have much more to say. I' m a person who speaks directly. The interview is there if you want to listen to it in its entirety... and not just certain snippets."

‌



It was during an interview with Spanish radio station Onda Cero that Rodri sparked headlines. "I'd like to return (to Spain), yes, obviously," the ex-Atletico star declared. "For me, La Liga is where I started. I still follow it, it’s true not as much as before, but I still follow it."

Rodri also admitted that the Premier League is his 'weakness', despite winning the title four times with City. "I think it's a thrilling league but at the same time very demanding, meaning it pushes you to the limit," the 29-year-old explained.

Should Rodri leave Manchester City? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Rodri felt that his comments were taken out of context (Image: David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty Images)

"I've been there for seven years now, and I'm noticing the passage of time, but for the moment I'm very happy there. I'm currently recovering from an injury, and what worries me right now is my feeling, my level, how to get back to my previous level.

"Not the contract issue, that will come, especially with a World Cup coming up, which is crucial for reaching my level. Right now, I'm free, well, obviously I have a year left on my contract. Obviously, there will be a point where we’ll have to sit down and talk, have a conversation."

Football.title: Thomas Tuchel deals Harry Maguire a brutal reality check with John Stones exception made
Football.content:
Thomas Tuchel deals Harry Maguire a brutal reality check with John Stones exception made

Harry Maguire is back in the England squad for the first time in two years, but the Manchester United defender is still facing a significant battle to force his way to the World Cup

View 3 Images Harry Maguire was back for England during their draw with Uruguay at Wembley

Thomas Tuchel is ready to give John Stones a sick note until the World Cup. But Tuchel then warned Harry Maguire is still well down the pecking order for places on the plane to the United States this summer.

‌



Stones, who will be 32 in May, has managed just four Premier League starts this season and missed England’s friendly win with Uruguay after suffering yet another injury blow.

‌



However, England boss Tuchel is willing to make an exception for “ world class” Stones despite his injury issues because he is such a big fan of the Manchester City centre half.

‌



That flies in the face of Manchester United defender Maguire with Tuchel insisting he is at least FIFTH in line behind Stones, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi and even Chelsea ’s crocked centre half Trevoh Chalobah who could be out injured for another month.

Tuchel said on Stones: “He's obviously very upset and at the moment he gets my full support because it helps him more than putting more pressure. He was ready to play for City in the last weeks. He was ready to play.

Harry Maguire slams England referee for allowing horror tackle on Phil Foden READ MORE :

“He played in the Champions League and he played in the FA Cup, but he was not used in the league. But he played enough for me to be important for us. So strong in training again, like every time I see him. I think he's a world-class player.

‌



“But he has a lot of credit in the bank with me. So let's hope that he gets fit because it's most important that he finds his confidence.

“What is the exception? I don't know yet, but if you come to the World Cup you should be fit.

“So the exception of the rule means that he does not start a lot. I can see that because I'm a big fan and I know what he brings to the team in terms of personality, attitude and quality game understanding.”

‌



View 3 Images John Stones' minutes over the last year have been limited to injuries (Image: PA)

Maguire will stay with the England camp until Tuesday’s friendly with Japan after winning his first cap since September 2024 against Uruguay.

The United centre half earned plaudits for his performance against Uruguay but has been left in no doubt that he is down the queue for places.

‌



Tuchel added: “I got exactly what I thought. To be honest, yeah. Solid, solid central defender play. That's what he does. Very good on the ball, very calm, strong in the air and in the weapon for set-pieces.

“I haven't changed my mind but I see other players I like to start for us, I see other players ahead with a different profile. I see Ezri Konsa ahead, I see Marc Guehi ahead. It's no secret. I see Trevoh Chalobah on the level of mobility was slightly ahead of him.

View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel has said numerous players are ahead of Maguire in the pecking order (Image: ITV Football)

‌



“Also John Stones but he had injuries so he needed to come in camp. I needed to meet him in person to see how he acts within the group. It will be interesting now to see how he acts within the group. He will stay with us.

“Like I said, he has an asset. of course, that he can also be super-important in a tournament, in knockout football, in defending a lead and chasing a game with crosses and long throw-ins. and set-pieces.”

Football.title: Thomas Tuchel admits Uruguay blocked England's request for World Cup preparation
Football.content:
Thomas Tuchel admits Uruguay blocked England's request for World Cup preparation

This summer's World Cup will see teams be able to take designated water breaks during games to combat the sweltering temperatures - and Thomas Tuchel is a fan

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel is a fan of water breaks, but was blocked from using them against Uruguay

Thomas Tuchel insists World Cup water breaks are a good idea - but revealed Uruguay stopped using them at Wembley.

‌



France boss Didier Deschamps spoke out this week against the idea which will see games stopped in the summer midway through each half to allow players to be rehydrated.

‌



Deschamps argued that they have the potential to stop the flow and momentum of the game and is a bad idea even in the searing heat and conditions in North America.

‌



But Tuchel is in favour even if he says they will change the dynamic of games during the tournament. He also plans to use them as a chance to speak to and coach his players.

Thomas Tuchel deals Harry Maguire a brutal reality check with John Stones exception made READ MORE :

England boss Tuchel said: “I think I like them. I can speak to my players. Get a little bit of quality time with my players and can encourage them or change something.

“Does it change the game? Yes, 100%. It's almost in quarters. We asked for a water break this time but Uruguay denied it. They didn't want us to have it.

‌



“It gives us just a chance for interaction, for giving a bit of advice, for encouragement but also to the opponents. I think it's necessary and me as a coach, I will make use of it.”

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel was happy with Adam Wharton's contribution

Meanwhile, Tuchel praised Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton for his contribution as a half time substitute against Uruguay as he proved he can play against top opposition.

‌



Tuchel added: “He provided what he provided. There were some very good moments. We wanted to go through the middle more with him when he came on. But he also had some crucial balances on both sides of the story.

“We need these tests to see them actually against top players in midfield competing. Because only then we know. And this is what we got.”

Football.title: Noni Madueke injury latest as England boss Thomas Tuchel issues worrying update
Football.content:
Noni Madueke injury latest as England boss Thomas Tuchel issues worrying update

Noni Madueke was forced off in the first half of England's 1-1 draw with Uruguay on Friday night and left Wembley in a knee brace, handing Arsenal a major injury scare

View 2 Images Noni Madueke has injured his left knee (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

England boss Thomas Tuchel has admitted he is “worried” Noni Madueke has suffered a bad injury. Madueke left Wembley with his left leg in a brace in what will be another massive concern for Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

‌



Arsenal now face an anxious wait on the extent of Madueke’s injury as he appeared to have injured his knee in the challenge by Uruguay’s Rodrigo Aguirre.

‌



Tuchel says he is also hoping it is not too serious, but the signs did not look good for the Arsenal winger who was substituted before half time. Concerned Tuchel said: “I'm worried, of course. Very sad and upset and hopefully it's not a big injury.”

‌



Tuchel was also upset that VAR did not intervene after the strong challenge inside the Uruguay penalty box. He said: “It was the tackle. I think it was on the edge, the tackle, within the box. But they didn't check it.”

Noni Madueke injury fears as Arsenal ace seen in knee brace after England vs Uruguay READ MORE :

Jude Bellingham rages as Thomas Tuchel angrily complains after England vs Uruguay READ MORE :

Tuchel did praise Madueke’s performance up until then as the Arsenal winger faces a battle with West Ham’s Jarrod Bowen for a place in the World Cup squad. Tuchel said: “He started well, he was full of energy, he was ready to go.

‌



"And I think against a team like Uruguay, who rely on one-against-ones, to isolate them, he makes the spaces open up and he could have been a key player for us, which he is.”

That will be of little comfort to Arteta who has a mounting injury list with Eberechi Eze already having pulled out of the England squad with a calf issue which could keep him out for up to a month.

View 2 Images Arsenal face a nervous wait on Noni Madueke's injury (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



They have Mikel Merino also out with a foot injury which could keep him out for the rest of the season while Jurrien Timber missed the Carabao Cup final and is a concern.

Incredibly, six players in total pulled out of internationals with Leandro Trossard, Gabriel and William Saliba all pulled out of the March camps with their respective nations. The final one was Martin Odegaard as the Arsenal and Norway captain recovers from a knee issue but hopes to be back after the international duty.

Football.title: Sabalenka beats Gauff to retain Miami Open title and complete 'Sunshine Double'
Football.content:
Defending champion Aryna Sabalenka beat hometown favourite Coco Gauff in ‌the Miami Open final to join an exclusive club by completing the coveted 'Sunshine Double'.

World No 1 Sabalenka, who reached the final without dropping a set, won 73 per cent of her first-serve points and faced just two break points en route to a 6-2 4-6 6-3 victory in a rematch of ​the 2025 French Open final won by Gauff.

Sabalenka ‌is only the fifth woman to win the Indian Wells and Miami titles back to back, a ​feat known as the 'Sunshine Double' given the tournaments' respective locations in California and Florida.

Sabalenka raced out to a 2-0 lead but Gauff, ​from nearby Delray Beach and appearing in her ⁠first Miami final, got on the ⁠board with a love hold and then repelled three break points in her next service game to ‌get to 3-2.

But Sabalenka did not lose focus and eventually went up a double break on the world No 4 before closing out ‌a dominant opening on her serve.

There was very little to separate the two players in the middle set which remained on serve until Gauff broke Sabalenka for the only time in the match to force ⁠a third set.

Sabalenka broke Gauff to open ​the decider, held at love in two consecutive service ​games to go 5-3 up and then sealed the ​victory with her fourth break of the match when Gauff sent ⁠a backhand wide.

The Belarusian joins Iga Swiatek (2022), Victoria Azarenka (2016), Kim Clijsters (2005) and Steffi Graf (1994, 1996) as the only women to complete the 'Sunshine Double'.

The Belarusian ⁠also improved to 23-1 on the ​year, her only loss coming in the Australian Open final ​at the hands of Elena Rybakina, whom she went on to beat in the Indian Wells final and ‌Miami semi-finals.

Football.title: Tuchel names four centre-backs ahead of Maguire in pecking order
Football.content:
England boss Thomas Tuchel has appeared to deliver a big blow to Harry Maguire's World Cup chances by insisting he is still at least the fifth-choice centre-back.

Maguire looked to have strengthened his case for being on the plane to North America in the summer as he delivered a commanding performance on his return to the national team set-up in Friday's 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay.

It was his first appearance under Tuchel and he played the second half as captain in a polished display that has characterised his England career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tuchel was less than happy with referee Sven Jablonski's performance during England's draw with Uruguay

The German acknowledged the Manchester United defender's strengths, but said he remains behind Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi, John Stones and the injured Trevoh Chalobah in the pecking order.

"I got exactly what I thought, solid, solid central-defender play," he said. "That's what he does. Very good on the ball, very calm, strong in the air and in the weapon for set-pieces.

"I haven't changed my mind, but I see other players I like to start for us, I see other players ahead with a different profile.

"I see Ezri Konsa ahead, I see Marc Guehi ahead. It's no secret. I see Trevoh Chalobah on the level of mobility was slightly ahead of him.

"Also John Stones, but he had injuries, so he needed to come to camp.

"I needed to meet him in person to see how he acts within the group. It will be interesting now to see how he acts within the group

"Like I said, he has an asset, of course, that he can also be super important in a tournament, in knockout football, in defending a lead and chasing a game with crosses and long throw-ins and set-pieces."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Saturday Social panel discuss which No 10s make England's World Cup squad and who misses out

Asked whether he would be in the squad if it had to be named now, Tuchel said: "If, if, if. We don't need to name the squad tomorrow. He did a good game.

"He did what he does for Man Utd. He did it straight away. I'm very happy with him. To be honest, I haven't changed my mind. I got everything I expected from him.

"If I have to name it tomorrow, we have a lot of injuries, he could be in it. Who else would be there in the centre of defence?"

Tuchel: I'm a big fan of Stones

Image: Maguire (left) will be competing for a spot at the World Cup with John Stones

Stones was not involved against Uruguay after feeling his calf in training as the 31-year-old's frustrations with injuries continue, and he will play no part in Tuesday's friendly against Japan having been sent back to Manchester City for treatment.

The defender has played just five times for his club since the November international break and is struggling to get a consistent run of games.

Despite that, Tuchel says he has "credit in the bank" and described him as "world class".

Tuchel was asked whether he would make an exception for Stones with regards to his lack of playing time and he said: "I don't know yet, but if you come to the World Cup, you should be fit.

"So when he came [to camp], he was fit. He did not have a lot of minutes, but he has a level of game understanding.

"So the exception of the rule means that he does not start a lot. I can see that because I'm a big fan and I know what he brings to the team in terms of personality, attitude and quality game understanding."

In addition to Stones' withdrawal, the Football Association said Aaron Ramsdale, Fikayo Tomori, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Adam Wharton, Noni Madueke, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka were leaving the England camp before the Japan match at Wembley.

Image: Maguire heads at goal during the draw against Uruguay

Sky Sports' Lewis Jones reporting from Wembley after England's 1-1 draw against Uruguay:

When the England team was announced, one of the key decisions that perhaps got overlooked was the return of Maguire to the England fold. But Maguire is used to that when turning out for his country.

This is a player completely underrated for the consistency of performance he has shown during England's most successful ever period of results. He was always the first name on the teamsheet for Gareth Southgate for good reason. And on his first start since 2024, it was like he had never been away, coming up big in key moments in the match just like he has done throughout his England career.

He always offered a threat in the opposition box, played intelligent passes through the lines to set up attacks and even had time to ping a 70-yard pass into the path of Jarrod Bowen.

England needed him with the last kick of the game too as he threw his body in the way of a goalbound shot in injury-time. His experience of major tournaments, along with his affinity with the shirt surely now makes him a certainty to make the 26-man squad.

England host Japan in another friendly at Wembley on Tuesday; kick-off 7.45pm.

That will be the final chance for Tuchel to look at his players on the international stage before he announces his World Cup squad at the end of the season.

England then have World Cup warm-up matches with New Zealand and Costa Rica before their tournament opener against Croatia on June 17.

Football.title: Leigh snatch golden-point glory after O'Brien drop goal
Football.content:
Gareth O'Brien of Leigh celebrates kicking the match-winning drop goal

Gareth O'Brien scored a golden-point drop goal to earn Leigh a dramatic 21-20 victory over Toulouse.

Leopards looked to be heading for just a second Betfred Super League victory of the season when they led 20-0 but the French side fought back impressively to force extra-time with a last-gasp penalty.

O'Brien kept his nerve in front of the posts, though, to clinch a much-needed win for the hosts three minutes into the first added period.

Leigh were irresistible in the opening 20 minutes, with Josh Charnley twice running through to score, while Innes Senior's acrobatic effort saw him touch down in the other corner.

Liam Horne then broke through the middle for a try under the posts but Toulouse gave themselves hope for the second half when Romeo Tropis burst over in the 37th minute.

A great pass from Olly Ashall-Bott sent Benjamin Laguerre in 10 minutes after the break, and the gap was down to two points when Laguerre drove over again moments after Ryan Brown had been sin-binned for Leigh.

Toulouse overturned a 20-point deficit to force extra-time with an incredible comeback

Brendan Hands was then denied a try for offside but Toulouse forced extra-time when Jake Shorrocks, who had kicked all three conversions, calmly slotted over an 80th-minute penalty,

The visitors seemed to have the momentum but Leigh were brave on the restart and earned their rewards.

Relieved Leigh boss Adrian Lam told Sky Sports: "We made it difficult for ourselves. I thought a soft try just before half-time gave them some hope and momentum, and the whole second half was all theirs. Grateful we got through in the end. A much-needed win."

Opposite number Sylvain Houles admitted: "It's a hard one to take. We gave a 20 points head start. It's three times now and we cannot be happy with that every time. It's such a shame because the boys managed to find the energy to get back into the game. I'm disappointed for them."
