News.title: Swingers group plans six-hour X-rated party based on hit animated children’s film aimed as kids as young as eight
News.content:
SWINGERS are gearing up to take part in an X-rated party based on an Oscar-winning children’s animated film.

Partner-swapping couples will dress up as characters from KPop Demon Hunters — a Netflix movie aimed at children aged as young as eight.



The six-hour S&M night, called K-Pop Dom Hunters, is open to fans of BDSM, fetishism and role play.



The event is also said to be suitable for “brats” — people who enjoy misbehaving for punishment — and those who like dominance and submission (D/S).

The adult event will be held at the Purple Mamba club in West Bridgford, Nottingham, close to Trent Bridge cricket ground and Nottingham Forest’s City Ground stadium.

The members-only party takes place next Friday from 8pm until 2am.

Couples pay £35, but single women can get in for just £15.

The website reads: “Kinksters, brats and good girls — we need you to help us.

“Join forces to slaaaayyyy. Embrace your inner K-pop star with a dress code inspired by cosplay and cuteness.

“Suitable for all fet lovers, kinksters and d/s dynamics alongside players and slayers.”

It adds: “Let’s defeat those evil doms once and for all — or at least try to.”



Membership costs £40 for a year, or £150 for a VIP subscription. Students can join for £20 per annum.

KPop Demon Hunters is an animated musical fantasy film which tells the story of three Korean pop stars who moonlight as demon hunters to protect their fans.

It was released on Netflix last June and became its most watched original title with more than 500million views.

Golden — a song from the film — has topped the charts in 30 countries, with 1.51billion streams on Spotify.

It won Best Original Song at the Oscars, while the film itself scooped Best Animated Feature.

News.title: Meet the real-life canine crime-buster who’s been run over, stabbed & shot at as he rescues celebs’ pups from dognappers
News.content:
PET thieves are cashing in on the soaring value of stolen dogs – but canine crime-buster Wayne May is hot on their trail.

With thefts now reaching five a day across Britain, the former Army bomb disposal expert is on a mission to reunite distraught owners with their pets — even though it can mean risking his life.





Wayne, 55, has been run over, stabbed and shot in the leg during his daring rescue missions. He has even dressed up as a postman.

He said: “I have used drones, military-grade thermal imaging cameras and advanced surveillance techniques to recover the animals.

“It’s always fulfilling to get them back. It’s worth the risks — I hate dog thieves.”

In the past 16 years Wayne has recovered more than 3,000 stolen dogs and secured hundreds of convictions against the thieves.

Among his past clients are ten “very famous” people, including actors and newsreaders, and Wayne said: “Celebrities panic slightly more than everyday members of the public, as they quickly think the worst because of their status.

“They are willing to pay thousands to get their pets back.

“We had one celebrity that was deliberately burgled because of who they are and their chihuahua was taken. We trawled websites and saw when the dog came up for sale.

“We went along to a big block of flats in Islington in North London, and scanned lots of puppies with a microchip reader as we were pretending to stroke them.



“Then we knew we had the right dog and bought it back for the owner.”

In the ten years to 2024 more than 23,000 dogs were stolen in Britain.

The most targeted breeds are French bulldogs, which have had a resale value over £3,000, followed by Staffordshire bull terriers, chihuahuas and Jack Russells.

DogLost, the UK’s largest free lost-and-found dog database, recorded a 170 per cent rise in thefts from 2019 to 2020. In 2024, 1,808 dogs were reported stolen, roughly five a day.

This month seven dogs were stolen from dog walker Abigail Booth’s van in Failsworth, Greater Manchester.



She said she went into an “instant panic” when she heard her van “wheel-spinning” away from a client’s house with the dogs inside.

Earlier this year a drone search found stolen bulldog Tilly in Ayrshire, hundreds of miles from her Manchester home, five months after vanishing.

And a Cavalier King Charles spaniel and her four five-week-old puppies were snatched from their home in Coney Weston, Suffolk.



Most thefts are orchestrated by highly organised gangs who quickly sell the dogs on to new owners.

It was after Wayne’s spaniel and terrier show dogs were stolen in 2018 that he turned detective. The dogs were in their kennels on his farm in Dartford, Kent, when he heard them barking from inside his house.

He said: “It was unusual, they never barked. I looked outside to see someone nicking my dogs.

“I rushed out, tried to chase them, but they jumped into a black Range Rover, ran me over, then sped off.

“I was so devastated — and angry.”



With help from the police, DogLost and local wardens, Wayne eventually recovered two of them.

And after photos were circulated, a third, a terrier called Beau, was spotted being taken on to a ferry to the Isle of Wight from Southampton — 100 miles from where they were stolen.

Wayne added: “The police obviously can’t spend hours on helping because they don’t have the resources — it doesn’t compare to murder, rape or drug-dealing.

“But DogLost, who I now work with, bent over backwards to help.”

After hours of painstaking research Wayne eventually identified the thieves and mounted round-the-clock surveillance of their property.



He was never able to secure a conviction for the theft of his dogs but he did manage to gather enough evidence to see all of those involved jailed for other crimes.

He said: “We discovered two were people-smugglers, others were drug- dealers and we watched and recorded as some stole cars.

“Arrests were made and they went to prison. I didn’t get my dogs back but I did get some justice.”

In 2023 Wayne helped to trace a cocker spaniel called Honey, who was stolen from her owners’ home in Meopham, Kent.

STARS’ ANGUISH AS POOCHES SWIPED LIZZIE CUNDY offered a £5,000 reward for the return of her dog Alfie after he was snatched while being walked by a friend in London in 2023. The six-month-old Maltipoo was stolen in Belgravia by a couple in a silver car. Just days later, Alfie was reunited with the TV host after being handed in to a vets. Lady Gaga’s dog walker was shot and wounded as heartless thieves took two of her French bulldogs Koji and Gustav in Hollywood. A third bulldog, named Miss Asia, ran away and was later picked up by police. The stolen dogs were returned unharmed two days later after Gaga offered a $500,000 reward. Walker Ryan Fischer had part of his lung removed after the 2021 attack. The shooter, James Howard Jackson, got 21 years’ jail. Sheridan Smith was overjoyed to be reunited with Enid after the pooch was stolen from the actress’s London home in 2010. She asked Twitter followers for help and her pet was found – in Barking, East London. Strictly contestant Gemma Atkinson was distraught when a dog was stolen from her local animal sanctuary in Bury, and asked her army of Instagram followers to help find missing Buddy in 2017. Panicked by the social media buzz, the thieves left the dog at a vets. Actor Martin Clunes offered a £2,000 reward to help find his pal’s beloved dog Pippin in 2016. The partially deaf Yorkshire terrier/poodle cross was snatched in a raid on owner Jane Wilson’s Leicestershire home. BBC journalist Rory Cellan-Jones’ pet collie Cabbage vanished when a dog walker’s van was stolen in London in 2021. All six dogs were later found wandering together.

He discovered she may have been taken to a puppy farm for breeding, and said: “It was a rural property.



“I and a team set up surveillance to watch around the clock, with night vision and tents.

“We gathered amazing evidence and got the puppy farm shut down and the people involved banned from keeping dogs, but Honey wasn’t there.”

After leafletting and stories in the local media the family heard that Honey might be in the Ashford area.

Wayne said: “We tracked her down via seven different properties throughout Kent.

“The thieves were moving her on constantly while waiting for her to come into heat so they could breed from her.



“We used different cars to watch, we even dressed up as postmen to walk down the street and we had a couple of real postmen who wore hidden cameras for us when they delivered, so if a dog came to the door we would see it.

“When we found the property we watched around the clock again for seven days and eventually saw Honey in the garden at about 5am.

“We approached and stroked her and managed to scan her to get the microchip number.

“On this occasion it would have taken five days to get a warrant, so we returned the next night and lifted her over the fence and got her back.



“I will never forget placing her back in the owner’s garden and texting them to say she was home.

“I could hear joyful screams from outside. A little while after that they moved with her to Spain, as they were so affected by what happened.

“When a dog is stolen, owners understandably get very stressed, and emotion can get in the way of dealing with the police.

“The information we give the police is 99.9 per cent correct, whereas an owner may be more confused.

“We handle things calmly, we know what people are going through, as most of us are victims ourselves.”



Every owner is grateful — and Wayne stays in touch with some of them.

He said: “In 2020 in North London three pugs were stolen from a nurse. She came home in the middle of the night and found her house had been ransacked and the dogs were gone.

“Two of them were found nearby but little Snuggles had gone. We managed to track him down via his microchip.

“We knew where it was last scanned and we emailed vets in the area.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Eventually we found it had been bought by an innocent new owner. We called the police and got Snuggles back after six weeks.



“She rings me on the anniversary of when the dogs were stolen every single year to say thank you.”

News.title: Soham monster Ian Huntley’s daughter left ‘disgusted’ after cops ask her if she wanted to pay towards his funeral
News.content:
SOHAM monster Ian Huntley’s daughter told of her fury after cops said she may have to pay towards his funeral.

But disgusted Samantha Bryan said she has refused to be involved in any way.





Samantha, 27, said: “I had nothing to do with him in life and now I want nothing to do with him in death.”

“I don’t want to pay for any funeral and I wouldn’t want to go to a funeral for him.”

She said she met two police officers on March 17, ten days after Huntley — who she never met — died following a battering in jail with a metal bar.

During the 30-minute meeting, she told them she did not want any involvement in his funeral or to receive his ashes.

She previously told The Sun on Sunday she wanted them to be flushed down the toilet.

Samantha, from Cleethorpes, Lincs, was told she could be liable if funeral costs exceeded £3,000.

She said: “They asked if I wanted to take on the responsibility, purely because I am his ­biological daughter.

“They mentioned if I did there would be quite a bill involved. I said ‘no’.



“He does not deserve the dignity of a funeral after what he did. I don’t want any involvement.”

Her mum Katie Bryan, 45, who was groomed and abused by Huntley, said: “Being asked if she wanted to be involved in this monster’s funeral and if she wanted to pay was the final ­indignity of having Huntley as a ­biological father.

“Even in death, he is a blight on her life.”

Huntley, who killed ten-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman in 2002, will have a basic cremation after all his family turned down the offer of a state-funded funeral.

Samantha and Katie now say his ashes should be dumped at sea like Moors Murderer Ian Brady in 2017.



Fellow Frankland jail lag Anthony Russell, 43, is charged with Huntley’s murder.

Huntley’s inquest begins next month.

News.title: McSweeney’s stolen phone and Rayner’s stamp duty show there’s one policy this Labour government will NEVER U-turn on
News.content:
THE withering spotlight of truth can bring even the high and mighty to their knees – just look at the ruin the Epstein files have inflicted on Lord Mandelson and the former Prince Andrew.

All that excruciating social contact that went on long after the world knew that Jeffrey Epstein was a child abuser on a multi-millionaire’s budget.





All those embarrassing images of high times with Jeff.

Mandy and Andy are finished for ever because the shameful facts about their relationship with Epstein came out in the end.

No wonder this Labour Government gets its free-trade knickers in a twist trying to avoid all scrutiny.

No wonder potentially embarrassing evidence seems to get whipped away — as if by magic!

Health Secretary Wes Streeting has raised a few wry eyebrows with his claim that he has “disappearing messages” on his phone — although Wes previously released texts he exchanged with Peter Mandelson when he wanted to distance himself from his old chum.

Suggesting that some of Streeting’s messages do not disappear when it suits our Wes.

And isn’t that fishier than a Finding Nemo boxed set?





And it seems almost comically convenient — doesn’t it? — that Morgan McSweeney, the Prime Minister’s former Chief of Staff, should have his iPhone stolen just weeks after disgraced Peter Mandelson had been sacked as British ambassador to the USA because of his links to Jeffrey Epstein.

At the time of the theft, Morgan was up to his ginger eyebrows in scandal, because it was widely known he had strongly petitioned to get his old mentor Mandy the grandest job in diplomacy — despite all the warning signs that it would end in tears.

Now the world will never peruse the potential political dynamite on Morgan McSweeney’s device — because it was fortuitously nicked.

As a lame excuse, the my-iPhone-was-stolen line is down there with “the dog ate my homework, Sir”.

And yet, I can just about believe Morgan probably really did get his phone swiped by a “black guy” in his “late teens” who shamelessly rode “up on the pavement to grab my phone and then cycled off on a bike”.

I believe it because 117,000 phones are stolen every year in Mayor Sadiq Khan’s lawless London.

What’s a lot harder to swallow, frankly, is that Morgan failed to mention to the police that he was a senior member of the PM’s staff, and that he accidentally gave them the wrong address for the theft, informing the 999 call-taker it was “Belgrave Street” rather than Belgrave Road — which is miles away.

You can’t help noticing that avoiding blame is the only Government policy that is never subjected to a U-turn.

When Angela Rayner got caught with her fingers in the stamp duty till.



When Rachel Reeves rented out her Southwark flat without the appropriate licence. When Morgan McSweeney conveniently had his handheld device snatched.

When Wes Streeting’s messages disappear — apart from the ones that distance him from his former chum, Lord Mandy.

Nobody ever takes any blame in this Government. It’s never ever their fault.

“Cock-up rather than conspiracy,” insists Streeting, claiming that our Government is really not duplicitous — just bloody useless.

That might be even worse.

Stardom was an art for legend Marilyn

ON June 1, it will be 100 years since the birth of Marilyn Monroe and, to honour Hollywood’s greatest icon, the National Portrait Gallery is staging a show.

What current star of stage, screen or streaming will have their 100th birthday honoured in a gallery?

Sydney Sweeney, below? Julia Roberts? Meryl Streep?



In the century since Norma Jean’s birth, the stars have shone just a little bit dimmer.

VETS will soon be required to cap the cost of prescriptions, publish price lists and provide itemised bills.

Pet-owning journalists have been quick to share horror stories of fortunes blown on their cats and dogs.

But there is another story to be told. Because I clearly recall the care, com-passion and kindness from vets that I saw when our family’s beloved dog Stan was dying two years ago.

Stan was out on the first walk of spring when he suffered respiratory tract failure – his breathing packed up.

We took him into a 24-hour vet at 3am on a Friday. By early Saturday evening we were holding him in our arms and about to say goodbye.

All the vets who cared for Stan did everything in their power to save him.

In the end, it was not possible. But I will be forever grateful. When he was finally at rest and we were leaving, I glanced back to see a young vet gently run her hand over Stan’s lifeless body.

One last stroke for our beautiful boy. I don’t think I have ever seen a gesture full of so much love.



Are our vet bills too high? You bet. But our vets are priceless.

Mad to dump Nadiya

DROPPING Nadiya Bychkova from Strictly has been described as the show’s producers shooting themselves in the foot.

It is more like shooting themselves in the head.

Nadiya is an elite athlete – a double world champion – with the face of a film star.

She is the Strictly dancer who looks like a model.

She is the only hoofer on the show who has star power off the dancefloor.

“Glamorous through-and-through and with a speed and attack that belie her lofty 5ft 8in frame, Nadiya Bychkova has long been one of Strictly’s greatest assets,” sighs dance critic Mark Monahan.

“She is one of those rare performers who heartily embraces the show’s garishness while staying just a fraction above it.

“I suspect Strictly fans will pine for her.”



For Strictly fans, it is not the past-their-best “celebrities” who are the stars of the show, it is the dancers.

Strictly producers have realised that dropping Nadiya is an act of spectacular self-harm.

So we are now assured that she is in talks to take a backstage role as a choreographer.

Not good enough.

If there was ever a dancer who was not born to be backstage, it is surely Nadiya Bychkova – a world champion in Ballroom and Latin ‘10’ Dance.

It is not too late for Strictly’s producers to admit they got this one wrong.

Nadiya would have celebrated ten years on the show with the series this autumn.

Strictly’s producers should bring her back – as a dancer – while there is still time.

Ban Ed, not oil

IN the middle of a global energy crisis, it is clearly STARK RAVING MAD for Labour to ban new drilling for oil and gas in the North Sea.

“Soft in the head,” says Kemi Badenoch.



I think that should be soft in the Ed Miliband.

ZACK'S BOOBY PRIZE WHEN he makes unfeasible claims about growth, Zack Polanski is the only politician who is probably not talking about the economy. In his old day job, Zack boasted he could enlarge a woman’s breasts with the power of hypnotherapy. For years, Zack claimed that his “hypnotitism” had been misrepresented by the Press – but now concedes he boobed. The original revelations in the Sun about his breast enlarging gift really did help his business, Zack admits. Now it is 10 Downing Street – or bust! But even if Zack never becomes PM, he will always be the biggest t*t in British politics.

HARRY KANE models England’s World Cup home match shirt – yours for £134.99.

Seems a bit steep.

But what I struggle to get my head around about that pricey England shirt is the solitary golden star.

All these years – a lifetime – and there is STILL only the one World Cup winner’s star on an England shirt?

Somehow that lonely little star is even more disturbing than that price tag.

Pair win in loss

OLEKSANDR USYK and Anthony Joshua are spending time together in Kyiv – training together, eating together, hanging out and sharing what they have both learned about loss.

The Ukrainian champ has been keen to show AJ what Ukraine has suffered in the last four years of war with Russia.

And, of course, Joshua was recently in a car crash in Nigeria that killed his two close friends, strength coach Sina Ghami and personal trainer Latif Ayodele.

There is no other sport in the world where two men who have been bitter rivals – Usyk fought AJ twice, beating him both times – could become the closest of friends.



“I really appreciate he’s here,” says Usyk. “He’s not my rival, he is my brother.”

Only in boxing.

News.title: My 7-year-old son’s plea for me to stop scrolling and why I know Labour’s screen time guidance is going to backfire
News.content:
THERE’S no doubt the Government has turned nanny state by saying kids under five shouldn’t be allowed any more than one hour a day watching the likes of CoComelon and Peppa Pig.

Education Secretary Bridget Phillipson hopes this guidance will help struggling parents “fighting a constant battle” with their children over too much screen time. I agree with the sentiment.





But it is possibly one of the most ridiculous things I’ve ever heard.

An adult telling a five-year-old what to do should be child’s play.

And if the meddling politicians wanted to interfere, they should have properly stamped their feet.

No pre-school kid even needs an hour of screen time every day.

Science indicates that shoving tots in front of an addictive, flickering screen for that long can damage developing brains.

Labour’s fresh guidance is likely to backfire, too.

They’ve given those idiot parents, who think Instagram and YouTube are educational, permission to ignore their kids for a full 60 minutes, totally guilt-free.

We’ve all heard about children rocking up at school trying to swipe at the pages of reading books, barely able to dress themselves or use a toilet because the only life lessons they’ve learnt come from a screen.





Now, the HR director of one of Britain’s biggest water companies says problems are seeping into adulthood, too.

Neil Morrison, HR director at water company Severn Trent in the Midlands, said around ten per cent of young people joining its apprenticeship programme had the numeracy skills of an 11-year-old.

And after years of being glued to TikTok, these poor teenagers are unable to even tell the time on a real clock.

How sad that their lives have been blighted before they face the real world.

You could blame the teachers, who should be telling kids from the age of about six or seven how to tell the time.

But when they’re busy changing nappies in reception, there’s a backlog that mounts up.

I feel so sorry for the next generation.

Without vital maths skills, they won’t be able to work out payslips, tax, National Insurance or budget for rent or food.

During Covid, kids were actually encouraged to use tablets more.

When we were all shoved into lockdown, they had to spend hours stuck to those brain-numbing devices to try to scramble together some sort of home education.



And now, up and down the land, kids are still using tablets instead of books and pencils for school work.

It is a vicious, never-ending cycle.

This fresh government guidance does talk some sense.

Tots under two don’t need to be on screens and parents should stop spending so much time on their own phones in front of their kids. I agree.

Brain-numbing devices

So many of us do it, me included. I wouldn’t dream of letting my seven-year-old son sit and scroll for an hour a day, but he sees me doing it from breakfast until bedtime.

I am ashamed to admit he’s even asked me at times to put my phone down.

Now we must all teach by example. A landmark case in America this week shows how vital that is.

Global giants Meta and Google were found liable for a 20-year-old woman’s addiction to Instagram and YouTube, which began when she was a child.

A jury in LA decided both tech companies knew their social media apps posed a danger to minors and ordered them to pay millions in damages.

They are planning to fight this landmark verdict.



It’s time for parents to do some proper parenting — stop tots going on YouTube and tweens watching tablets at the dinner table to try to prevent the teens from doomscrolling.

We must take responsibility before it’s too late.

Because now that the bad platforms have been sued, the floodgates will open.

And those kids whose brains have been tortured by tablets will come for bad parents next.

Robot’s melted the ice maiden Melania

MELANIA TRUMP took the unusual step of nearly cracking a smile as she walked into a summit this week.

The notoriously frosty United States First Lady was not accompanied by the Donald but by a humanoid robot called Figure 3.

And this nifty little gadget “takes care of household tasks like laundry, cleaning, and doing the dishes, all autonomously”.

I would smile, too, if I had one of those.



TIGER A SORRY STATE

THIS is probably easier for me to say than for a die-hard golf enthusiast.

Tiger Woods is a selfish, reckless idiot who doesn’t deserve any sympathy at all.

He has been arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence after rolling his car in a crash near his Florida home.

Nothing can excuse potentially endangering the lives of others.

He’s been in plenty of crashes and has a prior conviction for reckless driving.

Maybe one of the most famous incidents was 17 years ago when he crashed into a tree and his cheating came out.

I met several of the women he’d slept with.

I was told he was self-obsessed and arrogant, a thrill-seeker who did what he wanted without caring about others.

He spent hundreds of thousands of dollars trying to keep these women quiet.



Tiger has apologised for his behaviour over the years.

But if you’re not going to learn from your mistakes, those are just hollow words.

He should use some of that money he likes to splash around on a full-time driver and rehab. He needs both.

PARTY LIKE FURY

EVERYONE loves a good wedding, don’t they?

And after seeing photos from the hen do of Tyson Fury’s daughter Venezuela, I can’t wait to see snaps of the big day.

She threw a party for 300 guests at Morecambe Football Club.

Venezuela arrived in a tiara and veil, plus a gold number that reminded me of C-3PO.

There were security guards, a gold-coloured cake, an enormous sign saying “bride”, a frozen yoghurt stand and flowers for all the guests.

Even her hubby-to-be was there, along with mum Paris. Plus, the obligatory film crew.

It will have to be one big fat gypsy wedding to beat that.



A.I. IS A REAL DEVIL

WE are living in a time when all of us worry about which jobs AI may nick in the future.

But here’s one that is needed more than ever as a result of the rise of AI – being an exorcist.

Not your average 9 to 5, granted, and not the easiest career to get into unless you have a passion for religion and the Catholic Church.

But apparently there is a recruitment crisis and more than 2,000 extra specialist priests are needed because devil worshippers are using AI.

The Pope is in a panic after being warned the new tech fuels “paganism and the occult”.

But before you knock out your CV (with the help of AI, obviously), there are some pitfalls.

Exorcists regularly get vomited on, sworn at and have nails spat at them by people who believe they are possessed by the devil.

Imagine that on your HR file.

COUNCILLOR Darryl Smalley summed up the fact that Fergie had been stripped of her Freedom of the City of York title, saying: “We don’t expect recipients of York’s highest honour to be saints. We simply do not want them to be best friends of convicted paedophiles.”



Well, quite.

RAT’S AN IDEA

GREAT excitement is spreading across Hampshire after a capybara called Samba escaped from Marwell Zoo near Winchester almost TWO WEEKS ago.

Kids are hunting for her and Lidl has offered free bananas to lure the roaming rodent home.

Meanwhile, bosses at the zoo are scrambling through archives to recall how they retrieved the last lot of giant rodents that escaped.

To lose one is careless – to do it again is just stupid.

Maybe they should try the same trick as Birmingham.

Don’t empty the bins for weeks and watch that giant rat come running.

News.title: Cops urgently searching for football fan, 18, missing for a week – as belongings found near stadium
News.content:
FIND HIM Cops urgently searching for football fan, 18, missing for a week – as belongings found near stadium

A MISSING football fan’s belongings have been found near a stadium after he vanished a week ago.

Paul Pike, 18, from Birmingham, had travelled to Derbyshire to watch his team play at Pride Park on Saturday, March 21, before he vanished.





The teen was last spotted outside the stadium less than 15 minutes after kick-off at around 12.43pm.

Paul was seen on CCTV walking a path that runs alongside the River Derwent close to the Millenium Way cut through, police said.

On Friday, Derbyshire Police said they had found items they believe belong to Paul near a path next to the stadium.

His family issued a heartbreaking statement this week saying they love him and are very concerned for his welfare.



It read: “Paul, you are not in trouble at all, we just want you home.

“Come home so we can look forward to the cricket season at Warwickshire and the rest of the season for the Blues.

“I will also sort out the away tickets for Hull.”

Cops have now launched an urgent appeal to anyone who may have seen the 18-year-old in the area at the time he was last seen.



A spokesperson said: “We are now appealing for anyone who was on the riverside path at around 12.45pm – in particular any cyclists who may have had an action camera that may have caught footage of Paul.

“We are keen to hear from anyone who has seen Paul, as well as anyone who was driving in the Pride Park area at the time who has dashcam footage.”

Paul is described as white, around 6ft 1in and of slim build with short dark brown hair and a beard.

He was last seen wearing a Sergio Tacchino tracksuit top which is grey on the top and black on the bottom, a Burberry patterned baseball cap, navy blue polo shirt and blue jeans.

Anyone with information has been urged to get in touch with the police, quoting the reference 1095 of March 24.

News.title: Houthis vow to continue strikes 'in coming days' after missiles fired in Iran war
News.content:
Houthis vow to continue strikes 'in coming days' after missiles fired in Iran war

The rebel group has pledged to 'carry out military operations in the coming days until the criminal enemy ceases its attacks and aggression'

View Image The Houthi rebels have launched 'direct military intervention' (Image: Getty Images)

The Houthi rebels have stated that they intend to continue military strikes 'in the coming days'. The Yemen-based group entered the Iran war earlier, firing missiles on Israeli military targets.

‌



The assault this morning was the group's first intervention in the US-Israeli war with Iran. A barrage of ballistic missiles was sent "targeting sensitive Israeli military sites".

‌



In a statement on Telegram tonight (Saturday), the rebel group said the action it was taking was to support "the resistance fronts in Palestine, the land of sacrifice and redemption; Iraq, the land of glory and defiance; Lebanon, the land of dignity and steadfastness; and Iran, the land of pride, honour, and defiance."

‌



It went on: "The Yemeni Armed Forces affirm that, in fulfilling their religious, moral, and humanitarian duties towards the free people of the nation on the fronts of jihad and resistance, and in response to the enemy's crimes against the people and the countries of the nation, they will continue, with Allah's help and reliance upon Allah, to carry out their military operations in the coming days until the criminal enemy ceases its attacks and aggression. "

Last night, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group was ready to join the conflict, adding that the group would enter the war if any new alliances join Washington and Israel against Iran and its ⁠allies, or if the Red Sea is used for "hostile operations" against Iran.

Article continues below

In 2025 Donald Trump launched a bombing campaign, with help from the UK, to prevent Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea. The assaults killed a number of top Houthi officials, but concluded when a ceasefire was negotiated.

Iran war LIVE: Ship carrying thousands of US marines arrives in Middle East READ MORE :

Houthis fire missiles from Yemen at Israeli targets as they join Iran war READ MORE :

An armed political and religious group, the Houthis champion Yemen's Shia Muslim minority, the Zaidis. They form part of the so-called Iranian-led "axis of resistance" against Israel, the US and the wider West - alongside with armed groups such as Hamas and Lebanon's Hezbollah movement.

There are concerns that the Houthis may target shipping in the Bab al-Mandab strait. The key shipping route lies between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, at the south end of the Red Sea.

News.title: Thomas Markle, 81, has found new love with nurse, 46, after health scare
News.content:
Thomas Markle, 81, has found new love with nurse, 46, after health scare

Thomas Markle, 81, reportedly met and fell in love with a nurse 35 years his junior after he needed life-saving surgery to remove a leg which saw him spend days in intensive care

View 3 Images Thomas Markle has found peace and love in the Philippines (Image: Thomas Markle: My Story/Channel 5)

Meghan Markle's dad said he feels 'blessed' after finding love with a much younger nurse who helped him recover from a life-threatening leg amputation.

‌



Thomas Markle, 81, met Rio Canedo, 46, while she was working in a rehab center in Cebu in the Philippines last December. Following a serious blood clot that saw him spend four days in intensive care, doctors had no choice but to remove his left leg below the knee.

‌



The nurse confessed that she had no idea who her partner was when she first met him - just that he had something of a reputation for being pretty "grumpy". The retired Hollywood lighting director claims his daughter ghosted him after she married Prince Harry in 2018.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas with his daughter Meghan, who is now the Duchess of Sussex (Image: Netflix)

He recalled the "heartbreak" at being unable to walk Meghan down the aisle during wedding after two heart attacks. "After everything that happened, I never imagined being in this position. But it is what it is," Thomas said.

Thomas, who has pneumonia, went on to tell The Mail on Sunday: "After enduring so many hardships, I’m so thankful to have met someone so kind and caring. She’s made such a difference in my life." During his stay in rehab, Rio made sure he followed a strict no-sugar diet and encouraged him to drink more water.

‌



"Even though I’m battling pneumonia, I don’t feel sorry for myself. I’m in good hands with Rio. She takes such great care of me. I live in a place where kindness is the norm," he said.

Rio went on to describe Thomas as a "complete gentleman, very kind and humorous," as well as being easy to get along with. Although his life is now filled with peace, it wasn’t always so.

View 3 Images Thomas said that Meghan has cut ties with him

‌



He has never met his royal grandchildren - six-year-old Archie and four-year-old Lilibet - and continues to mourn the strained relationship with Meghan. "I still don’t understand why she cut me off. I tried everything to reach out privately before going public, but it was like hitting a wall."

But a move to the Philippines - where life is "simpler" - has helped ease his mind. He is now grateful for his health and to those that have showed him kindness since being there.

When asked whether or not he'd visit the wealthy area of Montecito in California, where Meghan and Harry live - he just laughed. "What’s the point? I love Meghan, she’s my daughter, but I’ve accepted that some things can’t be fixed. I want to focus on the happiness I’ve found with Rio."

Article continues below

Despite being earlier days in the couple's relationship, Thomas hasn't ruled out marriage, though it hasn't been discussed yet. "For now, we’re just happy enjoying life together. Every day with her feels like a blessing," he said.

For now, he wants to show her the different places he worked at in Hollywood just as soon as his health improves. While he calls himself an "old man" who can't believe he's made it to his 80s and is content with treasuring every moment he has with Rio.

News.title: Brit chip shop owner blames Donald Trump for his price rises in scathing tirade
News.content:
Brit chip shop owner blames Donald Trump for his price rises in scathing tirade

Nassar Iqbal, who runs the Hot Spot in Billesley, Birmingham, said the conflict in Iran means everything is getting more expensive, including the meals at his takeaway

View 4 Images Takeaway owner Nassar Iqbal blames Trump for price rises (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS)

A takeaway owner has blamed "warmonger" Donald Trump as he warned Brits the price of a chippy tea is likely to rise.

‌



Nassar Iqbal, who runs the Hot Spot in Billesley, Birmingham, said the conflict in Iran means everything is getting more expensive. He said his views of the US president have changed due to the war in the Middle East.

‌



Posting on social media, the entrepreneur said: "I quite like Trump, he reminded me of how my dad was. Old solid bloke, old views But he’s come this time, and all he’s doing is creating more wars; he’s a warmonger. Look at what he’s done in Iran.

‌



"He's killed their president, he's killed the family, now the Iranian Prime Minister wants revenge. Come on, things aren't looking good at the moment, are they?"

Urgent warning petrol crisis is so dire drivers will face LIMITS at supermarket pumps READ MORE :

OPINION Mikey Smith Donald Trump's unhinged 24 hours as he randomly drops major announcement into weird speech

View 4 Images "Warmonger" Donald Trump to blame for price rises, says takeaway boss (Image: Aaron Schwartz - Pool via CNP/Shutterstock)

‌



When the war started, airstrikes on multiple Iranian sites and cities killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Now, as the US-Israeli war with Iran enters its fourth week, thousands of US military members have arrived in the Middle East.

Recognising tensions are escalating, Nassar also expressed unhappiness with PM Keir Starmer. Speaking to our sister title, Birmingham Live, he said: "Keir Starmer's getting involved as well, so we’ve all got to get involved. So the fish is going to start getting more expensive. The potatoes, the oil, everything is going to get more expensive People are going to say to me: ‘Uncle Nas is putting the price up'’ I'm not putting the price up. Blame Donald Trump and Keir Starmer for having these wars."

The conflict has already driven up average UK petrol prices to above 150p a litre. The increase in diesel prices outstripped that of petrol, the average reaching 177.68p a litre, the RAC said. Before the Iran war started, petrol cost 132.83p a litre on average, while diesel was 142.38p.

‌



4 View 4 Images Nassar is pictured outside his Birmingham business (Image: Emma Trimble / SWNS) 4 View 4 Images Petrol and diesel prices have rocketed in the UK recently (Image: Maureen McLean/Shutterstock)

The situation became so dire today that a former oil company boss has urged ministers to consider imposing driving restrictions. Nick Butler, the ex- BP head of strategy and former policy advisor to Gordon Brown, warned that quick action is needed to manage the growing fuel shortage. One solution he suggested involved limiting drivers to alternate days on the road, depending on their car’s registration number.

Article continues below

Mr Butler also floated the idea of employers giving staff an extra day off each week to help cut down on commuter traffic, easing the strain on the country’s fuel supplies. He explained: "If supplies are cut by 20 per cent, then someone is using 20% less."

He went on to tell BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "The government has to protect the key sectors of the economy – food supply, health service, schools and so on – and then it has to work out how it's going to manage the market for the rest of us."

News.title: King Charles orders Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor to clear out former Windsor home
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: King Charles orders Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor to clear out former Windsor home

Former prince Andrew has not returned to his old Royal Lodge home on the Windsor estate since being evicted, leaving staff to burn their own belongings so no trace of the disgraced ex-royal is left

View 4 Images King Charles has ordered his disgraced brother to completely vacate his old Windsor home by the weekend (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The King has given an order to former prince Andrew which has left aides in a race against time to remove any trace of the disgraced ex-royal.

‌



The monarch last month brought forward a deadline for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor to leave the 30 room Royal Lodge mansion, after he was repeatedly named in the latest tranche of files relating to the convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein.

‌



The King commanded his shamed brother to leave the Windsor home he had lived in for over 20 years, paying a peppercorn rent after signing an initial lease worth £7.5million in 2002. Andrew denies any wrongdoing.

‌



Royal aides have in the past few days been clearing out the remaining possessions from Royal Lodge, including the staff quarters where Andrew was waited on night and day by royal flunkies.

View 4 Images Disgraced former prince Andrew has been ordered to completely clear out his old Royal Lodge home in Windsor by the weekend (Image: NO CREDIT)

‌



A number of skips have been loaded and removed from the estate, with removal vans seen coming and going. Staff have also been setting fire to further unwanted belongings of their own.

One source said: “Andrew was told everything has to be out and absolutely nothing was to be left behind. He hasn’t been back to collect anything, leaving staff to Everything has to be out by the weekend and we’ve been told no trace of the former occupants or staff should remain.”

Palace sources insisted the burning of furniture and other items on the estate belonged to Andrew's former staff. The once busy Royal Lodge estate appeared largely deserted last week. Guards were not seen staffing the gatehouse at the entrance to Windsor Great Park, close to the gates of the disgraced royal's former home.

‌



Aerial photos showed a skip, full to the brim, close to the rear of the 30-room royal residence. Another yellow-coloured skip was also visible at the front of the estate, behind the front gates.

It was placed outside the quarters of some of Andrew's former servants, including one remaining staff member who formerly worked for the disgraced royal.

On Tuesday, the man, understood to be one of Andrew's former valets, was seen burning belongings, including furniture, on the grounds of the Royal Lodge estate.

‌



View 4 Images Removal vans have been a permanent fixture outside Royal Lodge since Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor was evicted by King Charles in February (Image: NO CREDIT)

On Wednesday, removal men were seen loading items, including a mattress, into two vans outside the man's home. The removals firm was JDL, which according to its website specialises in Television and Film Transport.

Online testimonials show the company previously worked on Netflix show The Crown, which charts the lives of members of the modern Royal family, including Andrew. Our source added: "The estate is like a ghost town as so many staff have left and it’s now pretty much empty.

‌



"Who knows when it will be done up as lots of building work is needed to bring it up to its former glory, like when the Queen Mother was in residence."

Andrew’s exit from Royal Lodge - along with his ex-wife Sarah Ferguson who lived with him rent free for much of the last two decades - cements his spectacular fall from grace.

The King has stripped away his round the clock security as well as his personal allowance. He will no longer have a valet at his disposal or be lavished with taxpayer cash, as he was throughout his pampered life.

‌



After finally having his titles and honours stripped away by the King last October, he was driven away from Windsor on Monday, February 2, and taken 132 miles away to Sandringham under the cover of darkness to avoid being seen.

The Mirror previously revealed how Andrew had to be granted permission to return to Windsor to clear out any extra belongings he had not previously removed or put into storage after he had heaped further shame on the royal family.

But he has not returned since he left and set up temporary home at Wood Farm on the Norfolk estate, where the late Prince Philip spent much of his final years. Andrew was photographed last weekend for the first time since his arrest, walking his dogs with security on the Norfolk estate.

‌



In the coming days he is expected to move into a nearby five bedroom cottage, Marsh Farm, which has undergone extensive renovations in order to make it habitable for Andrew.

New security fences have been erected with a Sky TV engineer seen installing television and broadband services. Royal sources have confirmed that the King has met the refurbishment costs himself due to his brother’s wrecked finances.

Last week, a mobile home was delivered to Sandringham to installed a huge mobile home on the Sandringham grounds, right next to his new home of Marsh Farm. Sources have confirmed the luxury caravan will be used for security staff, paid for by the King, to stay over when needed.

‌



View 4 Images A mobile home has been delivered to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's new home in Sandringham, Norfolk, where security staff can stay over (Image: Bav Media)

He will have access to a cook and a cleaner at his new home, but it is unclear who is meeting the cost. The King had already stripped away his brother’s permanent security detail as well as his allowance, leaving him reliant on handouts at the grace of the monarch, when he was dramatically arrested on his 66th birthday - February 19.

Officers from Thames Valley Police are investigating claims that the former prince had committed misconduct in a public office. Andrew was questioned for 11 hours by detectives assessing claims that he shared sensitive information with Epstein when he was a UK trade envoy.

‌



The allegations stem from documents released by the US justice department relating to Epstein and his links to the rich and powerful. Emails apparently sent by the King’s brother appear to show Mountbatten-Windsor sharing reports of official visits to Hong Kong, Vietnam and Singapore.

Another email appeared to send Epstein a confidential brief on investment opportunities in the reconstruction of Helmand Province, Afghanistan.

Andrew has always denied any wrongdoing or accusations against him, but has not directly responded to these latest allegations. In response to his brother’s dramatic arrest, the King expressed his “deepest concern” but said the “law must take its course”.

Article continues below

Buckingham Palace also said the police had the King’s “full and wholehearted support and cooperation” Pressure has continued to build on Mountbatten-Windsor to give evidence in the US over his relationship with the paedophile financier.

A top Democrat last week demanded he testify on Epstein as “service” after his decades-long friendship with America's most notorious paedophile.

Congressman Jamie Raskin, the leading Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, told The Mirror: “I would imagine that anyone as deeply involved as Prince Andrew clearly was would have a story to tell. I would think he would see that as some form of service, after being so disgraced by his involvement.” Andrew denies any wrongdoing.

News.title: 'Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's exile is complete - now he must do this one thing'
News.content:
'Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's exile is complete - now he must do this one thing'

King Charles ordered his disgraced brother - Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor - to clear out his former Windsor home, leaving him in exile with plenty to think about his next move

View 3 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is facing numerous allegations being probed by investigators in the UK and the US (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The Royal Lodge clearout marks the latest in a long line of humiliations for the disgraced former prince Andrew.

The King has made no secret of his stance on his brother’s spectacular fall from grace.

His recent statement expressing the “deepest concern” as well as stating clearly that “the law must take its course”, leaves no doubt that Andrew will not be protected by the institution.

After being arrested last month and questioned for 11 hours on allegations of misconduct in a public office relating to his time as a British trade envoy, Andrew faces 10 separate investigations by police forces and authorities across the country probing Jeffrey Epstein’s distressing crimes. Andrew vehemently denies anywrong.

View 3 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is facing numerous allegations being probed by investigators in the UK and the US (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Pressure is also continuing to build across the Atlantic, with campaigners from across the political divide in the United States as well as investigators tasked with combing through Epstein’s web of criminality, appealing to the ex-royal to do the right thing and tell them anything he knows about his peadophile pal.

There will be no sympathy for Andrew’s desperate position being evicted from his home and his finances in disarray after paying a £12million out of court settlement to his sex-abuse accuser, the late Virginia Giuffre.

While he has always denied the allegations that he sexually abused her on three occasions in 2001 when she was a 17-year-old trafficking victim of Epstein's, he must now finally do the right thing and find it within his conscience to tell detectives anything he know about the late billionaire's sick and twisted life.

As Andrew soon settles into exile in a far corner of the King’s Sandringham estate, more than 100 miles from where he has lived it up for the last two decades, he will have to become accustomed to a life far less luxurious to the one he has been accustomed to.

View 3 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's former Royal Lodge home, the 30-room mansion the King has evicted him from (Image: NO CREDIT)

The threat of further questioning by detectives in the UK and the US hangs over him like a dark cloud, as well as his banishment from a family whose name he traded off his entire life.

The King brought forward a deadline for Andrew’s eviction in February, owing to public outrage over his continued reference in the latest trance of Epstein files released by the US State Department.

Article continues below

Whatever Andrew had maintained in the past, his version of his friendship and severing of ties with the convicted sex offender, were laid bare with page after page of private emails and correspondence between the billionaire financier and the Duke of York who begged to be his “pet”.

At the centre of all of this must be Epstein’s countless victims, some who have added their own voice to appeal to Andrew to do the one decent thing he can and speak to US investigators probing Epstein’s crimes.

As he gets used to life outside the royal fold, a life now in complete disgrace owing to his own conduct, he will have enough time on his hands to think about finally making that call.

News.title: Donald Trump 'will go ballistic' if King Charles scraps visit - and he'll blame one person
News.content:
Donald Trump 'will go ballistic' if King Charles scraps visit - and he'll blame one person

Plans are afoot for King Charles to meet Donald Trump, the US President, at the end of April during a state visit, but pressure has mounted on the monarch to change his mind

View 3 Images Donald Trump reportedly wants King Charles' state visit to ahead (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Bullish Donald Trump "will go ballistic" if King Charles cancels his US state visit, it is understood.

‌



It is said the US President, 79, would also firmly put the blame on Keir Starmer whom he recently declared is "no Winston Churchill". The relationship between the two leaders has become strained since the British government initially declined to grant the US access to RAF bases for strikes on Iran.

‌



Things appear so bleak that Mr Trump would publicly take aim at Mr Starmer if King Charles' state visit doesn't go ahead. Pressure has mounted on the monarch to axe plans, following the President's vicious attacks on the UK. However, a source in Washington DC involved with the organisation of the visit told The Independent that Mr Trump “will go ballistic” if the visit is cancelled.

‌



And Washington’s ambassador to the UK has warned that it would be "a mistake" to reverse these plans. Warren Stephens said: "I think he will go and I think it will be a very meaningful trip for him (Charles)."

King Charles suffers awkward blunder during royal visit as aide rushes to help him READ MORE :

3 View 3 Images King Charles is set to head to the US next month (Image: Getty Images) 3 View 3 Images Mr Trump would be angry with Keir Starmer if the plans don't happen, it is said (Image: Jonathan Buckmaster)

‌



The warning comes after an expert claimed Mr Trump wouldn't ever be rude to King Charles, because the monarch is a personal friend. Historian and royal biographer Andrew Lownie called on Charles, 77, to go ahead with the trip as he believes the king will be able to persuade the US leader "to do things that might not be possible otherwise".

The historian suggested this could mean Charles would be able to convince Mr Trump to release the full, unredacted Jeffrey Epstein files, which would be admissible in any potential court proceedings.

Efforts by authorities and politicians, including Thames Valley Police and the Metropolitan Police, for the US to make these unredacted documents have, seemingly, hit brick walls despite public pressure.

Article continues below

But the visit is being overshadowed by the war in Iran and Donald Trump’s repeated criticism of Mr Starmer. Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said last week: "Keir Starmer should advise the King that the state visit to the US scheduled for April should be called off. At a time when Trump has launched an illegal war that is devastating the Middle East and pushing up energy bills for British families, it’s clear this visit should not go ahead."

And the chair of the Foreign Affairs Select Committee, Dame Emily Thornberry, recently told BBC Radio 4: "If it was to go ahead next month – the dates haven’t been confirmed, but everybody seems to think it’s going to be next month – it would go ahead against a backdrop of a war and that, I think, is quite difficult."

News.title: Boy, 13, dies in Grimsby after being hit by car while riding scooter as 2 arrested
News.content:
Boy, 13, dies in Grimsby after being hit by car while riding scooter as 2 arrested

The teen was taken to hospital with life-threatening injuries following the incident on Tuesday, with two men arrested as part of an ongoing investigation

View Image A 13-year-old boy has tragically died following an incident in Fairmont Road, Grimsby (Image: Google)

A 13-year-old boy has tragically died following an incident in Fairmont Road, Grimsby. The teenager was riding a self-propelled scooter when he was struck by a car on Tuesday (March 24).

Police have arrested two men as part of their investigation. An 18-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and attempting to pervert the course of justice, reports Grimsby Live.

A 41-year-old man has also been arrested on suspicion of perverting the course of justice. Both men have since been released, police said.

A Humberside Police spokesperson said: "At around 6pm, we received reports that a white Seat Ibiza was travelling on Fairmont Road before it is believed to have been in collision with a child riding a self-propelled scooter across the road. Emergency services attended, and the 13-year-old boy was taken to hospital for treatment to life-threatening injuries.

"Despite the efforts of medical professionals over the past four days, the teenager sadly died yesterday evening (Friday, March 27). Enquiries remain ongoing to determine the full circumstances around the collision.

Article continues below

"As part of these initial enquiries, we can confirm that an 18-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and attempting to pervert the course of justice. A 41-year-old man has also been arrested on suspicion of perverting the course of justice.

"Both men have since been released under investigation."

The spokesperson added: "Officers continue to appeal to anyone who may have witnessed the collision or has any information, including CCTV or dashcam footage from around the time the incident is believed to have occurred, to please contact us on our non-emergency number 101 quoting log 346 of 24 March."
